utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. May I remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone present

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to warn you again to pause between question and answer so that we will make it easier for the transcript and the interpreters. Sir, you're familiar with the fact that the military operations in Vukovar took place within the area of responsibility of the 1st Military District; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the wider context.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The 80th Motorised Brigade at the time was also one of the units of the 1st Military District; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 80th Motorised Brigade, after the third wave of mobilisation, was within the Operations Group South.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And what about the Operations Group South?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Operations Group South belonged to the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about the 24th Corps, to which the 80th Motorised Brigade belonged to before being resubordinated to the Operations Group South?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I presume the 1st Military District, because we communicated only through a short period of time with the 24th Corps, since we had two unsuccessful waves of mobilisation, and after the third mobilisation, after the battalions and artillery battalions were completed, we were sent out to carry out tasks. Therefore, we knew some other units that were resubordinated to us better than the 24th Corps, although we were trying to get more men from that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Is that from your personal experience or does that include the opinion of the other officers of the 80th Motorised Brigade who belonged to the 24th Corps throughout, even before the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When on the 21st of November --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, in September of 1991.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were sent away and told to report to the 24th Corps, and from there we were supposed to be deployed within the 80th Motorised Brigade as foreseen by the order on the sending of troops for temporary assignments. Unfortunately we were sent from Topcider directly to the area of Sid, and as officers we reported to the command of the 1st Infantry Guards Motorised Division there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you mentioned the 20th Partisan Brigade. Did that unit belong to the 24th Corps as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, I wasn't certain of that before I received the overview of the units and analysed it. According to my knowledge, it was a separate unit. When I was in the area of Vukovar, it was a neighbouring, an adjacent unit, all the way until the 18th of November, 1991. After having spent 45 days at the front line, the unit left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We mentioned the operations group. Would you agree with me that an operations group is a temporary or provisional formation comprising two or more corps or brigades to carry out specific tasks and that once those tasks had been completed the operations group is being disbanded. Is that in accordance with the military rules?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. And to me, it was something I learned there, because apart from the Operations Group South, there were similar formations of provisional nature. For example, the Tactical Group North. Some even called it the Operations Group North.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that by an order of the commander of the Operations Group South, as early as the 9th of November, 1991, commands of particular locations or settlements were ordered to be formed in order to protect the inhabitants and property there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found such orders in the archives of the military historical institute in 2003 in April.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. By that particular order commanders of settlements were ordered to abide by appropriate rules for garrison and barracks service, when commanding the settlements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the task or the aim of forming such commands, as is stipulated in the preamble of the order, was to carry out anti-sabotage and anti-terrorist protection of the units belonging to the commands in the area. Therefore, they were formed with a particular aim in mind, and later the operational part was carried out, in terms of their tasks. Depending on whether in a given settlement there were civilian authorities in existence or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In case there were civilian authorities, what was the situation then? Who was the competent person to carry out the tasks of securing peace and order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In case there were civilian authorities, then the military authorities, as regards such settlements, and as far as I can remember, were tasked with establishing military authorities to control the situation. Of course, in such settlements in which there were no civilian authorities, the situation was a bit more peculiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: According to the rules of garrison and barracks service, is one of the duties of the settlement commander to regulate discipline and order inside the garrison or barracks, and to inform the officers and heads of institutions that may temporarily happen to be in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before me I have certain provisions of the rules of the armed forces pertaining to that period, dating back to 1985. Chapter 3 pertains to accommodation and order, and chapter 4 on securing material and equipment. These are the two documents regulating this topic. And in certain of the items in those chapters, the rules exist concerning the establishment of settlement commands and the behaviour of the commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In those rules, does it say that a settlement commander should regulate order and discipline as well as the managing of the detention facility within the garrison or barracks compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is regulated by the rules, when it comes to securing property, personnel and material.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my next question might compromise the identity of the witness, so I would like us to move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We must then move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Before we go any further, I don't know what statements my learned friend is even referring to. I've got nothing from my learned friend. Could he perhaps indicate to -- what statements they are?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: We've receiving nothing from my learned friend at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my learned friend. I was quite clear in what I wanted to say. All the statements that I gave to the ushers just now are the statements that the Prosecution delivered to the Defence, and the witness confirmed yesterday that he gave all these statements in response to the question by Mr. Vasic, and these were statements that he gave to the military court in Belgrade to the ministry of the interior in Serbia, to the Belgrade court in the case trying war crimes, and I also gave him the statement that he himself gave to OTP investigators. Is my learned friend satisfied with my answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you, that's very helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to stop going through these statements, because we have not come to those statements yet, and answer the question that I put to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for your remark. I will do so. I wanted to check whether these were indeed statements that I mentioned, and I was going through these statements more out of curiosity than anything else. I apologise. You asked me when it was that I started preparing for my testimony. It is difficult for me to date that precisely. Unofficially it started in 1992 upon my return from the assignment I was carrying out. Officially, ever since 1997, when I heard that the first indictments were issued in respect of the Vukovar Hospital. The immediate preparations started when I was serviced with the first summons with the military court and so on and so forth, and to this date, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this mean that you have been dealing with these topics for nearly 15 years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In preparing for your testimony did you make use of the statements given by Vojnovic in different cases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In preparing for my testimony I used to a certain extent the statements given by not only Vojnovic, but other witnesses who were directly or indirectly in contact with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And these were statements that were published in the press.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you use the statements these witnesses gave before the court for war crimes in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't use those statements, except for the extracts that were published in the press.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to tell you that the trials were held in closed sessions, as far as these statements, some of these statements were concerned and that they must not have been published in the press, does this mean that you came by these statements otherwise, because yesterday in responding to Mr. Vasic's questions you said Vojnovic explained all that. How come you knew what it was that Mr. Vojnovic was going to say before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I referred to what Vojnovic had stated in the proceedings before the special court in Belgrade on the basis of press clippings. In view of the fact that I use the internet extensively, I was able to come by, among other things, your statement that you gave at the balcony after you were following these trials and this statement of yours was published in the press. And it included the following, and I'm paraphrasing: After what Vojnovic stated, he should replace my client in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's my opinion today. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what it is that has been bothering you for 15 years that you have -- that has made you prepare so thoroughly for -- on behalf of the Prosecution for these particular trials, and I mean you personally, what it is that bothers you as a person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I find this question problematic because I haven't been preparing against anyone for these 15 years. In the interview I gave to the ICTY investigators, please allow me to read that portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: No, please, I have an order in which I want to take my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: My learned friend asked a question. The witness surely must be allowed to answer the question in a way that he deems to be appropriate, and not to be interrupted because it doesn't suit my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please carry on, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Witness statement, item 2, page 0351-5011. "Representative of the -- the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia conducting this interview has informed me that the statement I'm giving may be used in the court proceedings before the International Tribunal for the Prosecution of Persons Responsible for Serious Violations of International Humanitarian Law Committed in the Territory of the Former Yugoslavia since 1991. "In this respect I wish to state that I would prefer to appear as a witness for the Defence. However, I agree to appear as a witness of the Office of the Prosecutor, I request that I be granted protection measures when testifying in the ICTY courtroom in The Hague, Netherlands, including image and voice distortion, perhaps even a closed session." And somewhere else I also pointed out that already given a statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe this is quite sufficient, thank you. May I proceed? Because I do accept that your motive was the one as you read it now. You have the statement that you gave to the investigating magistrate of the military court in Belgrade, it is before you. It is marked with number 1. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You stated there, you can merely follow, that on the 19th of November, on page 4, paragraph 1, of English version, page 5, paragraph 2, this is something you testified to yesterday in response to my learned friend's questions. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. Closed. Private, I should say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 28th day of April, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.06 p.m.,
